title: Positional Encoding — Telugu + English Learning
subtitle: Original English Diagrams, Formulas, Tiles, Code remain unchanged. Questions, Options, Explanations modern Telugu + Englishలో.
hero:
POSITIONAL ENCODING · NEW VISUAL LESSON

Words say what. Positions say where.

Transformers need a way to tell who comes first, next, and last—even when the same words appear in another order.

questions.stem: Transformerలో Positional Encoding అంటే ఏమిటి? Self-Attentionకు Word లేదా Token Order తెలుసుకోవడానికి Extra Position Information ఎందుకు అవసరం?
questions.figure:
VISUAL EXPLANATION

Where each word sits matters

A token embedding describes the word. Position information tells the model where that word appears.
options: Positional Encoding Word Meaningని Random Vocabulary IDతో Replace చేసి Token Content Ignore చేస్తుందంటుంది. Position, Meaning Separate.
Position Encoding Token Order ఇస్తుంది; Same Words Different Orderలో Attention Roles Distinguish చేస్తుంది.
Repeated Words Delete చేసి Unique Vocabulary Only Keep చేస్తుందంటుంది. Repetition, Order Lose అవుతాయి.
Transformerని RNNలా Words One-by-One Read చేయాలని Force చేస్తుందంటుంది. Parallel Processing Still Possible.

VISUAL EXPLANATION

The same five words can tell opposite stories

Without position signals, ordinary self-attention has no built-in order. Changing word order changes meaning.
options: Without Positions Same Words Different Order Confuse; Position Signal Subject/Object Distinguish చేస్తుంది.
Vocabulary IDs Alone Who Chased Whom Always Reveal అంటుంది. Words Same అయితే Order Missing.

Subject/Object Remove చేసి Both Sentences Identical చేస్తుందంటుంది. Position Signal Difference Preserve చేయాలి.

Tokens and positions meet before self-attention

In the original Transformer, token embeddings and position vectors are added together before attention. Modern methods vary.

questions.technicalExplanation:
Detailed explanation: NumPy Broadcasting Positions Column × Frequency Pairs, Even Sine, Odd Cosine; PyTorch float32 Convert చేసి Matching Token Embeddings Add. d_model=4 pos0 [0,1,0,1], pos1≈[0.8415,0.5403,0.01,0.99995]. Classic Additive, Not RoPE. Source Original Runnable Code Below Unchanged.
import numpy as np
import torch

positions = np.arange(4)[:, None]
frequencies = 10000 ** (np.arange(0, 4, 2) / 4)
pe = np.zeros((4, 4))
pe[:, 0::2] = np.sin(positions / frequencies)
pe[:, 1::2] = np.cos(positions / frequencies)

pe_tensor = torch.from_numpy(pe).float()
token_embs = torch.zeros((1, 4, 4))
sequence = token_embs + pe_tensor.unsqueeze(0)
print(np.round(pe, 4))
print(sequence.shape)  # torch.Size([1, 4, 4])
